status_note: Real EXTERNAL production adaptation of the xstream 1.4.18 default-deny break, found by GitHub mining and VERIFIED with a full 3-state differential over the repo's untouched production source (Maven harness; the repo's own Gradle+SWT build was bypassed, not the code). Causal link is also explicit in-repo (comment + version).
verified_by: 3-state differential (Maven 3.9.11, JDK 17) via scratchpad/xstream-tvrenamer-harness on real src/main source
discovery_method: Phase 2 external mining via GitHub commit search (q='xstream allowTypes 1.4.18' and 'xstream ForbiddenClassException'), then per-commit file/diff inspection to keep only src/main (production) adaptations.

library.version_provenance: The repo's real dependency update was xstream 1.4.9 -> 1.4.20, made in commit fa98c37 'Modernize: Java 17, Gradle update, and Windows EXE workflow' (bumped the version AND rewrote build.gradle from the old ivy/compile setup). That bump crossed the 1.4.18 default-deny boundary. The differential BASELINE uses 1.4.17, not 1.4.9, because xstream 1.4.9 (c.2014) does not run on JDK 17 (ExceptionInInitializerError, unrelated to the BBC); 1.4.17 is the newest pre-1.4.18 version that runs on JDK 17, so 1.4.17 vs 1.4.20 cleanly isolates the 1.4.18 change.

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: direct dependency; bump and adaptation in separate commits
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: Commit fa98c37 bumps xstream 1.4.9 -> 1.4.20 (crossing 1.4.18); the allowlist adaptation follows at b236f68e. The break was live in-repo from fa98c37 (parent-of-fix 16803ddb already declared 1.4.20 with no allowlist) until the fix. A genuine adaptation-to-a-change.

bump_source.comment: Break characterized from BUMP (apache/logging-chainsaw). TVRenamer is an independent client exhibiting the SAME break in production preference-persistence code.

behavioral_break.mechanism: xstream 1.4.18+ default-deny: fromXML on a non-allowlisted class throws com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException.
behavioral_break.affected_production_path: org.tvrenamer.controller.UserPreferencesPersistence.retrieve(Path) -> xstream.fromXML(in) -> (UserPreferences). retrieve() catches only IOException, so ForbiddenClassException (a runtime exception) propagates.
behavioral_break.live_before_fix: The dependency bump (xstream 1.4.9 -> 1.4.20) landed at fa98c37 WITHOUT an allowlist, so the break was live in production from fa98c37 until the fix at b236f68e (multi-commit pattern: bump at fa98c37, adaptation at b236f68e). At the fix's parent commit 16803ddb the build already declared 1.4.20 with no allowlist.

adaptation.repo_note: A fork of tvrenamer/tvrenamer with active independent development; some commit messages look tool-generated and author dates are not reliably chronological — trust git ancestry, not dates.
adaptation.bump_commit: fa98c37 (xstream 1.4.9 -> 1.4.20, bundled with a Java 17 + Gradle modernization — NOT an isolated dependabot-style single-dependency bump)

adaptation_decoupled_from_update.note: The adaptation was made in a SEPARATE commit from the dependency update, and NOT bundled into the same change unit — the version bump is at fa98c37 while the allowTypes fix is at b236f68e.
adaptation_decoupled_from_update.pr_note: Neither commit was made via a pull request — both were committed directly to the branch (GET /commits/{sha}/pulls returns none for both). So the update and the adaptation are not only different commits but were never grouped in a single PR.
adaptation_decoupled_from_update.gap_commits: 15 commits (bump fa98c37 -> fix b236f68e is ahead_by=15; 14 intervening commits, almost all build modernization: remove Ant/Ivy, SWT fixes, jlink/shadow/CI). The fix's direct parent is 16803ddb.
adaptation_decoupled_from_update.gap_author_dates: fa98c37 authored 2026-01-11T17:11:32Z, b236f68e authored 2026-01-12T22:48:54Z -> ~1 day 5.5 hours in AUTHOR time.
adaptation_decoupled_from_update.gap_committer_dates: Both committer dates are 2026-02-02T02:52 (16s apart) — the whole 15-commit chain was replayed/rebased in one batch, so committer dates do NOT measure real development time. Trust commit distance + author dates, not committer dates.
adaptation_decoupled_from_update.caveat: This fork's history looks tool-generated (conventional-commit prefixes; entire chain committed in one ~16s burst), so wall-clock gaps are unreliable as evidence of human reaction time. The STRUCTURAL fact — update and adaptation are separate commits, 15 apart, in no shared PR — is solid.

adaptation.location: production static initializer on the shared XStream instance
adaptation.in_repo_causal_evidence: The added code is prefixed with the comment: '// XStream 1.4.18+ requires explicit security permissions' — the maintainer explicitly attributes the change to the xstream security boundary, so this is NOT proactive hardening (contrast ActiveMQ AMQ-6013).
adaptation.summary: Allowlisted the deserialized preferences type (and the whole org.tvrenamer.model package by wildcard) on the PRODUCTION XStream instance used by UserPreferencesPersistence, satisfying xstream >=1.4.18 default-deny. This is the production-side fix the chainsaw case lacked.
adaptation.later_removal: Commit eeba95a6 (2026-03-05) 'Replace OkHttp and XStream with JDK built-in APIs' later dropped xstream entirely — the same eventual trajectory as apache/logging-chainsaw.

verification.method: 3-state differential over the REAL production source, run via a Maven harness (scratchpad/xstream-tvrenamer-harness) that compiles the repo's untouched src/main/java, parameterises the xstream version, and runs one authored test that calls the production UserPreferencesPersistence.retrieve() on a realistic preferences XML. JDK 17; XStream needs --add-opens for java.base/{util,lang,lang.reflect,text,io} and java.desktop/java.beans.
verification.test: org.tvrenamer.controller.PreferencesBbcTest#preferencesDeserializeFromXml (authored; derived from the BUMP failing test LogPanelPreferenceModelTest#testLogPanelPreferenceModelSerialization).
verification.harness_notes: The test deserializes a preferences XML with no <pcs> element to isolate the target break: UserPreferences holds a non-transient java.beans.PropertyChangeSupport that is a SECOND forbidden type under 1.4.20 (TVRenamer's fix allowlists the domain types but not PropertyChangeSupport) and also has JDK-serialization fragility at 1.4.17 — an interesting partial-adaptation observation, but a confound for the domain-type differential. `mvn clean` is required between states (incremental compile skips recompilation after a git checkout).
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC with a real external PRODUCTION adaptation: baseline passes, the same production code breaks only under xstream >=1.4.18 with a ForbiddenClassException on the real domain type UserPreferences, and the client's production allowTypes/allowTypesByWildcard adaptation resolves it.
